claims.statement: On secp256k1-ecdlp (input T=[x]P0, x uniform in [0,n), no auxiliary powers) this package ports the judge-validated plain-track mu6 orbit-row walk (bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain ticket 5ecbf15) and repairs, after three rejections, every source-level defect the reviewers named. THE SUBMITTED SUCCESS IS 0.550999 >= the 0.39 floor, and it is MEASURED, not modelled, ON THE SAME CHALLENGE (verdict 40b720e2 point 1): evidence/pair-census.json draws ONE challenge block xt (its SHA-256 is in the file), then for each of 3,200 sets runs the walk TWICE at the same budget with only the walker coins redrawn (starting coefficients (a,c) and the walker coin stream are fresh per run), scores a set solved when either run solves, measures 1,817/3,200 = 0.5678125, and takes the one-sided Clopper-Pearson lower bound 0.5532103 (the CP helper is Monte-Carlo calibrated at this n and p: coverage 0.9515, and the k=n closed form 0.05^(1/n) is checked). The reviewer's same-target form 2p-p^2 gives 0.5672827 against the measured 0.5678125 (diff +0.00053), so the measured event is solving the GIVEN challenge in either of two runs. The first v17 draft resampled xt and therefore measured the different-challenge event (2E[p]-(E[p])^2, larger by Var(p(Q))); that draft's 0.560408 is withdrawn. Minus the 2.211e-3 debits (transport, pool overflow, relation failure, detector abort, escape failure) the design success is 0.550999. THE CHARGE IS EXPLICIT: W2 = 2*W, exactly +1.000 bit, every term doubled rather than shared (ledger.py's W2 row). THE LAG-3 PATH IS FAITHFUL AND PROVEN TO FIRE. census_v20n.walk_arm now owns the whole step: it runs qwalk.step with the DP gate off and no run counter, applies EVERY substitution from the SAME pre-step tuple (class,a,c) the step advanced from, applies the run counter/restart to the union of both triggers, and RECOMPUTES the report gate on the class actually reported (v16's arm mixed post-step a/cc with the pre-step canon and kept the stale mask). The lag-3 trigger is successor class == class two steps back, which in a 3-cycle c_a->c_b->c_c->c_a is exactly the closing step. Firing proof (evidence/lag3-firing.json): in a small universe (q=20011, R=8, 3336 classes) 24 of 96 starts have a period-3 lag-1 trace; on those starts the lag-3 channel fires 150 times, the lag-1 arm fires it 0 times, 24/24 planted starts stop being period-3, and invariant violations are 0 in both arms. Production census (3,200 trials x 16 walkers x 1,687 steps, two shipped seed blocks): no-escape control 0.0050/0.0044; escape lag-1 0.2825/0.2897 (CP-95 0.269404); escape lag-1+lag-3 0.3228/0.3316 (pooled 0.32719, CP-95 0.309200). The 3-cycle channel is removed: lag-1 leaves 2,872/2,847 trials in a period-3 trace, lag-3 leaves 0 in both blocks (residual moves to period >=4), with 8,066/8,085 lag-3 fires per block and 0 sampled invariant violations. On secp256k1 that repair is worth +0.040 absolute success, not the bls template's +0.0006. PRODUCT COUNT: spec_window_secp executes 8 partial products (4 at i+j=3, 4 at i+j=4; i<=3 so (4,0) does not exist), not 7; selector.py carries PRODUCTS_V1=8 and asserts the measured (8,3) at import, and the row is priced 35 insn instead of 31. STEP_INSN = 152 (index 35, v0 24, v2 subtraction 4, argmin/selects 12, sign+key 12, orbit slot 7, loads/stores 20, coefficient update 9, checkpoint 10, lag-1 escape 6, lag-3 escape 4, batch inversion 1, counters 7, meter 1); price 1 + 152/1000 = 1.152 at C=1000 (this track's protected normalization; the bls C=2000 is used nowhere). W FORMULA: the cost model is total work = walkers x steps-per-walker x step-price, so W = (1 + 152/1000)*(S_OPS + 2^60) + EXTRAS with S_OPS = ceil(A_H1*S0) = 2^126.72144016; v16's prose A_H1^2*S0^2 would be 2^126.7 LARGER than the charge, so the code was right and the sentence is now the sentence of the code, both readings printed in ledger.py's docstring. KERNEL PRICE, STRUCTURAL ONLY: this package claims NO disassembly measurement. v16 stated 92 instructions "by disassembly" with no artifact, v17a shipped a static span (95) and v17b a corrected kernel with an executed count (287), and ALL of them are withdrawn because the v17a/b kernel did not pass its own reference test at full width (verdict b86f973b point 3). M_insn = 97 is a STRUCTURAL count (16 mul-adds at 5.5 insn each plus 9 insn setup and conditional subtract); it enters only TABLE_BUILD_REF and INV_INSN inside EXTRAS, where +-5 insn moves W by 2^-113 bits, so no part of the claim depends on it. restart_count.py takes the same constant and regenerates evidence/restart-count.json, so the stale 92-instruction price the reviewer found there is gone (fresh_ref 714.07 -> 752.82). Arithmetic: log2 S0 = 126.69996043, log2 W (one run) = 126.92594600, w=2 +1.00000000, log2 W2 = 127.92594600, claim 127.926. HONEST LIMITS: no production transfer argument is claimed for the single-run rate, and the two-run statistic inherits that gap -- it is measured at production shape (visits/sqrt(N) 1.009444 vs ledger 1.009696, dev 2.5e-4) in a scalar quotient simulation with q=4.29e9, R=64, 16 walkers, DP 2^-5, not on secp256k1 with R=2^20, 2^20 workers and DP 2^-60, so comparable trapping, DP recovery, cap and restart behaviour are NOT established; the run-to-run correlation is not modelled (measured p_set sits 0.00053 above 2p-p^2, disclosed); the cycle census is a trace-period statistic, not a terminal basin period; meetings beyond the 1,687-step cap are censored, not extrapolated; and 127.926 does not rank (frontier 126.338). The goal of this round is an honest floor-met posture that survives review, not a leaderboard move.
